flags.title: Quad soreness
flags.detail: watch for discomfort during easy runs. Recovery pace: keep heart rate in zone 2, avoid hard effort. Thanksgiving 10K plan: start low mileage, gradually build. Heart‑rate drift: note increases on easy days. Sleep: aim for 7–8 hrs to support recovery.

answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer: After the marathon, give your legs two full weeks of very light running.  Start with 3–5 mi easy runs on the first week, keeping heart rate in zone 2 and listening for any new pain.  In the second week you can add a short 5‑mile easy run, then a 6‑mile run that is still mostly zone 2.  This gives you a solid base for the 10‑K in five weeks.  In weeks 3–4 of that window you can add a moderate‑pace run (7–8 mi) and then a tempo or race‑pace 4‑mi effort in week 4, finishing with a easy run in week 5.

new.analysis: This week is a two‑week recovery phase after the marathon. The athlete still reports quad soreness and a blister, so a hard session would risk re‑injury. Replacing the Wednesday quality run with an easy run keeps the load low and allows the body to heal while still providing movement. The rest of the week remains light, maintaining 80% easy effort and no additional hard work.
